paper: Founou LL, Founou RC, Allam M, Ismail A, Essack SY (2022). Genome Analysis of ESBL-Producing Escherichia coli Isolated from Pigs. Pathogens 11(7):776.
context: n=11 clonally-related pig/abattoir ESBL E. coli from Cameroon and South Africa; independent replication (Coverage 10/10, Agreement 7/10, Verdict PARTIAL) reproduced CTX-M-15 = 6/11 with exact carrier identity and 10/11 MLST, with residual discrepancies in single-allele beta-lactamase composition (PN256E8 CTX-M-15 vs CTX-M-55; +1 CTX-M-15+TEM-1B co-carrier).

open_questions.q: How is the CTX-M-15 / CTX-M-14 / CTX-M-27 population structure distributed across IncF (F1:A2:B20 / F2:A-:B-) versus IncI1/IncI2 plasmids in sub-Saharan African pig-farm ESBL E. coli, and does the IncF-CTX-M-15 pig lineage in Founou 2022 share plasmid backbone (RepA / pMLST) with the well-characterised human clinical IncF-CTX-M-15 pandemic?
open_questions.basis: This replication verified CTX-M-15 in 6/11 with carrier identity and reproduced the presence of PlasmidFinder Inc-types, but did NOT reconstruct which resistance gene sits on which plasmid contig (short-read abricate can enumerate replicons and BLA genes but not physically link them). Founou 2022 attributes IncF replicons to several CTX-M-15 carriers but the exact CTX-M-15-bearing plasmid pMLST for pig isolates in sub-Saharan Africa is not established by short-read data.
next_steps: Long-read (Nanopore R10.4 / PacBio HiFi) or Illumina+Nanopore hybrid re-assembly of the 6 CTX-M-15 carriers (PN017E2II, PR010E3I, PN027E6IIB, PN027E1II, PN091E1II, PR085E3) to close plasmid replicons.
Run MOB-suite / plasmidSPAdes / Unicycler-hybrid to co-locate blaCTX-M-15 with its Inc replicon, and pMLST-type IncF plasmids (F:A:B allele triplet).
Compare closed pig-farm CTX-M-15/IncF plasmid backbones to public Enterobase/PLSDB human clinical IncF-CTX-M-15 plasmids (BLASTn identity, backbone gene synteny).

Also probe for CTX-M-14 / CTX-M-27 - the Founou 2022 cohort found CTX-M-1/-14/-55 in the non-CTX-M-15 isolates; whether CTX-M-27 (the East-Asian ST131-C1-M27 variant) is absent from African pig herds or simply under-sampled remains open.

open_questions.q: Is there directly-observed pig-to-human clonal transfer of CTX-M-15-producing E. coli in these Cameroon/South Africa abattoir settings, and what cgMLST / core-SNP distance threshold demarcates a genuine zoonotic transmission event from parallel acquisition in the same one-health environment?
open_questions.basis: Founou 2022 samples both pigs and abattoir workers; the isolate labels (PN* pigs vs PR* workers/carcass) suggest a paired epidemiological design, and replication confirmed that pig and human-adjacent isolates share STs (e.g. ST2144 appears in PR209E1 / PR246B1C). But co-carriage of the same ST is not the same as a demonstrated transmission chain; the replication did not run cgMLST or a core-genome SNP tree across the 11 isolates.
next_steps: Run chewBBACA cgMLST (Enterobase ecoli scheme, ~2360 loci) or Enterobase HierCC on the 11 assemblies, tabulate pairwise allele distances between pig-source (PN*) and human/abattoir-source (PR*) isolates within the same ST.
Run a core-genome SNP tree (Snippy / Parsnp) on same-ST pig-vs-worker pairs; apply a <10 SNP threshold (the widely-used clinical outbreak cutoff) to flag candidate transmission events.
Cross-reference candidate pig-worker transmission pairs with the metadata (same abattoir? same shift? same day of sampling?) to test whether SNP-close pairs are epidemiologically close.
Contextualise against public E. coli from African human clinical sources (Enterobase, PathogenWatch) to check whether the pig lineages are already circulating in local hospitals.

open_questions.q: What on-farm antimicrobial-use practices (which drugs, at what doses, prophylactic vs therapeutic vs growth-promoter) drive the observed CTX-M-15 dominance in Cameroon vs South Africa pig herds, and would a stewardship intervention (e.g. WHO-CIA-class withdrawal from feed) measurably reduce ESBL prevalence within one production cycle?
open_questions.basis: Founou 2022 is a descriptive genomic survey; it establishes prevalence and gene content but does not attempt causal attribution to specific husbandry drugs, and no intervention arm exists. Replication reproduces the prevalence signal but of course inherits the same causal gap.
next_steps: Retrospective farm-level AMU (antimicrobial use) survey at the sampled abattoirs and their supplier farms - which 3rd/4th generation cephalosporins, tetracyclines, sulfonamides, colistin are used, and at what animal-mg/kg biomass equivalent (mg/PCU metric).

Prospective before/after intervention pilot: remove medically-important cephalosporin use from pig feed at one cooperating farm, keep control farms, resample ESBL prevalence at 3/6/12 months by selective plating + WGS on same protocol as Founou 2022.
Difference-in-differences analysis of ESBL colonisation prevalence and CTX-M-15 gene copy load (qPCR on caecal DNA) between intervention and control farms.
Assess ecological co-selection: even after cephalosporin withdrawal, does continued tetracycline / sulfonamide use maintain CTX-M-15-IncF plasmid frequency (linked-resistance rescue)?

open_questions.q: What is the true co-carriage risk of plasmid-mediated colistin resistance (mcr-1/mcr-2/mcr-3) alongside CTX-M-15 in sub-Saharan African pig ESBL E. coli, and are current abricate/ResFinder short-read pipelines reliably detecting mcr variants at the observed carriage rate?
open_questions.basis: The replication resistome panel (abricate ncbi+resfinder) enumerated qnrS1, aph(6)-Id, aph(3'')-Ib, tet(A), mph(A), sul2, dfrA - but neither the REPORT.md rerun table nor the paper headline highlights mcr-1/-2/-3 status. Given that (a) African pig herds have been epicentres of mcr-1 emergence since 2016 and (b) IncF/IncI plasmids that carry CTX-M-15 frequently also host mcr, the absence-or-presence of mcr in this cohort is an open, high-stakes question.
next_steps: Re-mine the 11 assemblies specifically for mcr-1 through mcr-10 using a pinned ResFinder DB and independent BLASTn against NCBI mcr reference alleles, at >=90% identity / >=90% coverage.
Phenotype-confirm any mcr+ isolate by broth microdilution colistin MIC (EUCAST breakpoint > 2 mg/L).
For mcr+ isolates, long-read close the mcr-bearing plasmid and test whether it also carries blaCTX-M-15 (co-selection risk).
If mcr is absent in all 11, run a power-and-detection-limit analysis: how many additional pig isolates would need WGS to bound sub-Saharan pig-herd mcr prevalence below (e.g.) 5% with 95% confidence?

open_questions.q: How systematically do sub-Saharan African pig-farm ESBL E. coli genotypes (dominated in Founou 2022 by CTX-M-15 on diverse STs including ST10/44/69/88/226/940/2144/4450) diverge from European pig-farm ESBL genotypes (historically dominated by CTX-M-1 on IncI1 and CTX-M-14 on IncK), and what does that divergence say about independent regional selection pressures vs. shared globalised swine-trade transmission?
open_questions.basis: Founou 2022's CTX-M-15 prevalence (54.54%) and the ST spectrum recovered here (ST10, ST44, ST69, ST88, ST226, ST940, ST9440, ST2144, ST4450) are strikingly different from the European pig-herd literature (EFSA/EURL-AR reports and e.g. de Been et al., PLoS Genet 2014; Ceccarelli et al., 2020) where CTX-M-1/IncI1 dominates. The replication verified the African pattern but did not perform the cross-continent comparison.
next_steps: Pull public pig-source ESBL E. coli WGS from Enterobase / NCBI SRA for European (Netherlands, Germany, France, UK), North American, and East-Asian pig herds, filter by isolation source = pig / porcine / swine.
Recompute CTX-M variant frequencies and ST distributions on a common ResFinder DB snapshot to remove tooling drift.
Test whether the CTX-M-15 vs CTX-M-1 dominance split correlates with regional 3rd-gen cephalosporin veterinary use intensity (OIE / WOAH ANIMUSE database).

Build a core-genome ML tree across continents to assess whether African pig CTX-M-15 lineages are independent emergences on the local ST background or descend from imports of the well-known human CTX-M-15 pandemic - i.e. is the pig herd the source, the sink, or a parallel reservoir?
